items.prompt: May I ___ your dictionary? I will return it tomorrow.
items.hint: The speaker receives something temporarily.
items.explanation: Borrow means receive something for temporary use.

items.prompt: Could you ___ me your pencil?
items.hint: The other person gives something temporarily.
items.explanation: Lend means give something for temporary use.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
choices: I borrowed a book from Maya.
I lent a book from Maya.
items.hint: Check the direction and preposition.
items.explanation: Borrow something from someone describes receiving it.

items.prompt: Please ___ me what happened.
items.hint: A person follows the verb directly.
items.explanation: Tell someone something uses a direct person object.

items.prompt: What did she ___?
items.hint: There is no person object after the gap.
items.explanation: Say can introduce the words or message without a person object.

items.prompt: He ___ a funny story to the class.
items.hint: This verb commonly goes with story.
items.explanation: Tell a story is the appropriate collocation.

items.prompt: I need to ___ my homework.
items.hint: Think of the usual verb with homework.
items.explanation: Do homework is the usual collocation.

items.prompt: Everyone can ___ a mistake.
items.hint: Think of the usual verb with mistake.
items.explanation: Make a mistake is the usual collocation.

items.prompt: Let us ___ a plan before we begin.
items.hint: The noun is plan.
items.explanation: Make a plan is the usual collocation.

items.prompt: The train leaves at 10. It is 9:45 now. We are ___.
items.hint: We arrived before the departure time.
items.explanation: Early means before the expected or required time.

items.prompt: The lesson began at 9. Tom arrived at 9:20. He was ___.
items.hint: He arrived after the start.
items.explanation: Late means after the expected time.

items.prompt: Please arrive ___ time for the interview.
items.hint: Use the fixed expression for being punctual.
items.explanation: On time means at the scheduled time.

items.prompt: I was ___ about speaking, so my hands shook.
items.hint: Choose a feeling that fits the physical reaction.
items.explanation: Nervous describes worry or unease.

items.prompt: After practising, she felt ___ enough to give her talk.
items.hint: The word describes belief in her ability.
items.explanation: Confident means feeling able to do something.

items.prompt: He had waited an hour and felt ___.
items.hint: He found further waiting difficult.
items.explanation: Impatient describes difficulty waiting calmly.

items.prompt: You can find a word meaning in a ___.
items.hint: Which reference book explains words?
items.explanation: A dictionary provides word meanings and other language information.

items.prompt: Please ___ the book by Friday so another reader can use it.
items.hint: Give it back to the library.
items.explanation: Return means give or take something back.

items.prompt: The book is due on Friday. Due means ___.
items.hint: Look at the deadline context.
items.explanation: Due here refers to the required return date.

items.prompt: Type the missing word: Can you ___ me your ruler?
items.hint: You are asking someone to give it temporarily.
items.explanation: Lend describes the giver action.

items.prompt: Type the missing word: Please ___ the truth.
items.hint: Use the usual verb with truth.
items.explanation: Tell the truth is the standard expression.

items.prompt: Type the missing word: I will ___ my best.
items.hint: Think of the fixed expression.
items.explanation: Do my best means try as well as I can.

items.prompt: The opposite of late is ___.
items.hint: Think about arriving before the start.
items.explanation: Early contrasts with late.

items.prompt: A person who believes they can succeed feels ___.
items.hint: The word begins with con-.
items.explanation: Confident describes belief in your ability.

items.prompt: Type the missing word: Please ___ the book to the library.
items.hint: Give it back.
items.explanation: Return fits the library context.
